title: Growing the grid: one knot for a new line, three for a filled cell
claim: On Young-diagram shapes the box-betweenness base is the cut system (d = 2 L1); a step starting a new line needs exactly one three-place knot, B(opposite corner, neighbour, new), unique; a filled corner needs exactly three, unique within L1 radius 2 (the unit square; computed in 4 x 4 and 5 x 5, not proved), and the unit-square parity alone also extends; totals are order-independent ((r+c-3) + 3(r-1)(c-1)); the states name every placement (withdrawn after referee R1, Block: equal states can have different placements; the states name only the new-line pair).
standard_statement: Halfspaces of median-closed subsets of Z^2 (Djokovic-Winkler classes) are the row and column cuts; set covers of the extension's bad states by three-place constraints.
prior_work: Djokovic 1973; Winkler 1984; Bandelt, Chepoi and Eppstein (squaregraphs); KNOT-ORDER-20261117-001.
completion_gate: Ticket B's census confirms every statement on the 4 x 4 box; the referee reviews the proofs.

validation.status: proof written before the freeze; checked by ticket B; refereed (R1: G1-G4 confirmed, G5 withdrawn)
validation.independence: cover search by brute force against the proofs; same task authorship

attained_result: G1-G4 proved; G5 withdrawn after referee R1 (Block); G3's local uniqueness computed, not proved.
